semin-durr:55-55.t: His saying: {لِذَنبِكَ}: It has been said: the maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its object, i.e. "for the sin of your community concerning you." The apparent meaning is that Allah says what He wills, even if it is not permissible for us to attribute a sin to him ﷺ.

semin-durr:57-57.t: His saying: {لَخَلْقُ السماوات والأرض أَكْبَرُ مِنْ خَلْقِ الناس}: The two maṣdars (verbal nouns) are annexed to their objects, and the fāʿil (agent) is omitted, namely Allah the Exalted. It is also possible that the second is annexed to the agent, i.e. "greater than what people create," meaning what they make. It is also possible that both are maṣdars standing in the place of "the created thing," i.e. what was created of them (the heavens and the earth) is greater than what was created of them (people), meaning their bulk is greater than their bulk.

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ المسياء}: «لا» is redundant (zāʾida) for tawkīd (emphasis), because when the speech became long through the ṣila (relative clause), the counterpart of "the believers" became distant, so He repeated «لا» with it for emphasis. He put "the believers" first only because of their adjacency to His saying «والبصير». Know that contrast comes in three ways. The first: that the corresponding item is placed next to what corresponds to it, as in this verse. The second: that the two contrasted items are both placed later, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {مَثَلُ الفريقين كالأعمى والأصم والبصير والسميع} [Hūd: 24]. The third: that the counterpart of the first is placed first and the counterpart of the last is placed last, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَمَا يَسْتَوِي الأعمى والبصير وَلاَ الظلمات وَلاَ النور} [Fāṭir: 19]. All of that is variety in eloquence. He put "the blind" first in negating equality because it comes after the attribute of blame in His saying {ولكن أَكْثَرَ الناس لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ}.
His saying: «تَتَذَكَّرون»: The Kufans read it with the tāʾ of address, and the rest with the yāʾ of absence (third person). The address is by way of iltifāt (shift of person) to the two mentioned groups after reporting about them, and the third person looks to His saying {إِنَّ الذين يُجَادِلُونَ}, and they are the ones to whom He turned in the reading with address.

semin-durr:62-62.t: His saying: {خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ}: The majority read it in the nominative, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it in the accusative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "by way of specification (al-ikhtiṣāṣ)." And Ṭalḥa read with the yāʾ of absence (third person).

semin-durr:63-63.t: His saying: {كَذَلِكَ يُؤْفَكُ}: i.e. like that deluding.

semin-durr:64-64.t: His saying: {فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ}: Abū Razīn and al-Aʿmash read «صِوَرَكم» with kasra on the ṣād, fleeing from the ḍamma before the wāw. A group read it with ḍamma on the ṣād and sukūn on the wāw, and I took it as a generic noun (ism jins) of «صورة», like «بُسْر» and «بُسْرة».

semin-durr:70-70.t: His saying: {الذين كَذَّبُواْ}: Several aspects are possible in it: that it is a badal (substitute) for the relative noun before it, or an explicative (bayān) of it, or a naʿt (adjective), or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or accusative (manṣūb) by way of censure. On these aspects, His saying «فسوف يعلمونَ» is a resumptive clause brought for threat. It is also possible that it is a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is the clause «فسوف يَعْلَمون»; the entry of the fāʾ into it is clear.

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His saying: {إِذِ الأغلال}: They allowed this «إذ» to be in the sense of «إذا», because what governs it is certainly future, namely «فسوف يَعْلمون». They said: just as «إذا» falls in the place of «إذ» in His saying, Exalted is He, {وَإِذَا رَأَوْاْ تِجَارَةً أَوْ لَهْواً انفضوا إِلَيْهَا} [al-Jumuʿa: 11], so «إذ» falls in its place. Something like this has already passed in al-Baqara at His saying {وَلَوْ يَرَى الذين ظلموا إِذْ يَرَوْنَ العذاب} [al-Baqara: 165]. They said: what made this acceptable is the certainty of the action's occurrence, so it was expressed in the form of the past. I say: there is no need to take «إذ» out of its original meaning; rather it remains on its indication of the past, and it is accusative (manṣūb) by His saying «فسوفَ يَعْلَمون» as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "they will know on the Day of Resurrection the time of the shackles being on their necks," meaning the time of the cause of the shackles, which is the sins they used to commit in this world; as if it were said: "they will recognise the time of their sins that put the shackles on their necks." This is a clear aspect; the most it involves is a free use of «إذ» by making it a direct object, and that does no harm, for the grammarians most of the time say "accusative by an implied اذْكُرْ (remember)," and in that case it can only be a direct object, since it is impossible for the future to govern past time. They also allowed it to be accusative by an implied اذْكُرْ, i.e. "remind them of the time of the shackles so that they fear and desist." These are three aspects, the best of which is the middle one.
His saying: «والسَّلاسِلُ»: The majority read it in the nominative, and there are three aspects in it. First: it is conjoined to «الأغلال», and the prepositional phrase is the predicate of both kinds, the prepositional phrase being intended as placed after; the implied form is: "when the shackles and the chains are on their necks." Second: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted because the predicate of the first indicates it. Third: it is also a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is the clause «يُسْحَبُون»; there must be a referent in it returning to it, the implied form being "and the chains — they are dragged by them," omitted because of the strong indication of it. So «يُسْحَبُون» is in the position of the nominative on this aspect. As for the two preceding aspects, it may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun intended in the prepositional phrase, and it may be resumptive.
Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ibn Waththāb and al-Musayyibī in his choice read «والسلاسلَ» in the accusative and «يَسْحَبون» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, active; so «السلاسلَ» is a fronted direct object, and he has conjoined a verbal clause to a nominal clause. Ibn ʿAbbās said about the meaning of this reading: "When they drag them, it is harder on them: they are made to do that and cannot bear it." Ibn ʿAbbās and a group read «والسلاسلِ» in the genitive, with «يُسْحَبون» passive. There are three interpretations of it. First: construal according to the meaning, its implied form being "when their necks are in the shackles and the chains"; since the meaning of the speech was that, the conjunction was construed according to it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its justification is that if it had been said 'when their necks are in the shackles' in place of His saying {إِذِ الأغلال في أَعْنَاقِهِمْ}, it would have been correct and sound; so since they are two expressions that alternate, He construed His saying «والسلاسل» according to the other expression. A parallel to it is:
3941 - مَشائيمُ ليسوا مُصْلِحين عشيرةً ... ولا ناعِبٍ إلاَّ بِبَيْنٍ غُرابُها
(Ill-omened folk, they do not set a clan aright, nor does their crow croak except of parting.)
as if it had been said «بمُصْلحين»." And it has been read «بالسلاسِل». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Its implied form is 'when their necks are in the shackles and the chains'; so it is conjoined to what is intended by the speech, not to the order of the wording, since its order involves an inversion (qalb), and it is like the Arabs' saying 'I put the cap into my head.'" In the codex of Ubayy: {وفي السلاسل يُسْحَبُونَ}. The Shaykh said after the statement of Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Zamakhsharī quoted above: "This is called conjunction by supposition (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-tawahhum), except that supposing the entry of the preposition onto «مُصْلِحين» is nearer than altering the structure of the whole clause, and the reading [here] involves altering the structure of the whole preceding clause. A parallel to that is the saying:
3942 - أجِدَّكَ لن تَرَى بثُعَيْلِباتٍ ... ولا بَيْداءَ ناجيةً ذَمُوْلا
ولا متدارِكٍ والليلُ طَفْلٌ ... ببعضِ نواشِغِ الوادي حُمُوْلا
(Do you truly think you will not see at Thuʿaylibāt, nor in a desert, a swift, easy-paced she-camel, nor [be] one catching up, while the night is still young, with laden camels at some of the valley's channels?)
The implied form is: 'you are not a seer nor one catching up.'" What these two said was preceded by al-Farrāʾ, for he said: "Whoever reads «السلاسل» in the genitive construes it according to the meaning, since the meaning is: their necks are in the shackles and the chains."
The second aspect: it is conjoined to «الحميم», having been placed before the item it is conjoined to; the discussion of this will come. The third: the genitive is by the implication of an omitted preposition, and this is supported by the reading of Ubayy «وفي السلاسل», and others read it «وبالسلاسل»; al-Zajjāj inclined to this. However, Ibn al-Anbārī rejected it and said: "If you said 'Zayd is in the house,' it would not be good to imply «في» and say 'Zayd the house (genitive)'." Then he mentioned al-Farrāʾ's interpretation and explained the reading by it, then said: as you say "ʿAbd Allāh disputed with Zayd, the two intelligent ones," with «العاقلين» in the accusative and in the nominative, because when one of them disputes with his companion, the other has disputed with him. This issue does not accord with the principles of the Basrans, who explicitly forbade it; among the Kufans only Ibn Saʿdān held it. Makkī said: "It has been read «والسلاسلِ» in the genitive by conjunction to «الأَعْناق», and that is a mistake, because it becomes 'the shackles are on the necks and in the chains,' and there is no sense to shackles being in chains." I say: his statement "by conjunction to «الأعناق»" is not granted; rather its genitive is according to what has preceded. He also said: "It has been said that it is conjoined to «الحميم», and that too is not permissible, because a genitive conjoined item does not precede the item it is conjoined to. If you said 'I passed by — and Zayd — ʿAmr,' it would not be permissible; in the nominative it is permissible, as in 'stood — and Zayd — ʿAmr,' and it is far-fetched in the accusative: 'I saw — and Zayd — ʿAmr' is not good; and no one has permitted it in the genitive."
I say: the apparent sense of his words is that it is permissible though far-fetched in the nominative, whereas they have explicitly stated that it is not permissible except by poetic necessity, with three conditions: that the conjunction does not come at the beginning, that the governing word is fully inflected, and that the item conjoined to is not genitive. They cited:
3943 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... عليكِ ورحمةُ اللَّهِ السَّلامُ
(… upon you — and the mercy of Allah — be peace.)
along with other evidentiary verses, while explicitly stating that it is restricted to poetic necessity.
The chain (al-silsila) is well known. Al-Rāghib said: "«تَسَلْسَلَ الشيءُ» means the thing quivered, as if a repeated slipping were conceived of it, so the repetition of its wording points to the repetition of its meaning. «ماءٌ سَلسَلٌ» is water that ripples in its place." Al-saḥb is dragging with violence, and al-saḥāb (clouds) is from that, because the wind drags it, or because it drags the water. «سَجَرْتُ التنُّورَ» means I filled the oven with fire and stirred it up; from it is «البحر المَسْجُور», i.e. the filled sea; and it has been said: blazing with fire. The poet said:
3944 - إذا شاءَ طالعَ مَسْجُوْرَةً ... تَرَى حَوْلَها النَّبْعَ والشَّوْحَطا
(Whenever he wishes, he comes upon a brimming pool, around which you see nabʿ and shawḥaṭ trees.)
So the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He, here {ثُمَّ فِي النار يُسْجَرُونَ} is: the fire is kindled with them, as in His saying {وَقُودُهَا الناس} [al-Baqara: 24]. Al-sajīr is the bosom friend who is ablaze (yusjar) in his friend's love, as they say: "So-and-so burns in the love of so-and-so."

semin-durr:75-75.t: His saying: {تَفْرَحُونَ}: [with] «تَمْرَحون» is of the category of al-tajnīs al-muḥarraf (altered paronomasia), which is when the difference between the two words lies in one letter.

semin-durr:76-76.t: His saying: {فَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى المتكبرين}: The specified item (al-makhṣūṣ) [of the verb of blame] is omitted, i.e. Hell, or "your abode." He did not say "evil is the entrance," because entering does not last; only abiding lasts, so He singled it out for blame, even though entering is also blameworthy.

semin-durr:77-77.t:
His saying: {فَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its origin is «فإنْ نَرَكَ», and «ما» is added to emphasise the meaning of the condition; for that reason the nūn was attached to the verb. Do you not see that you do not say «إنْ تُكْرِمَنّي أُكْرِمْك», but rather «إمَّا تُكْرِمَنِّي أكرمْك»?" The Shaykh said: "What he mentioned of the mutual necessity of the nūn and the redundant «ما» is not the doctrine of Sībawayh; it is only the doctrine of al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjāj. Sībawayh explicitly stated that there is a free choice." I say: although these rules have preceded in full, I mention them because they mentioned them, and in that there is also an alert and a reminder of what has preceded.
His saying: «فإلينا يُرْجَعُون» is not the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the first condition, but rather the apodosis of what is conjoined to it; the apodosis of the first is omitted. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«فإلينا يُرْجَعُون» is attached to His saying «نَتَوَفَّيَنَّك», and the apodosis of «نُرِيَنَّك» is omitted, its implied form being: 'If We show you some of the punishment We promise them, namely being killed on the day of Badr, then so be it; and if We take you before the day of Badr, then to Us they will be returned and We will take the severest revenge on them.'" I say: something like this preceded in Sūrat Yūnus, with the Shaykh's discussion of it, so let it be consulted. The Shaykh said: "Some of them said: the apodosis of «فإمَّا نُرِيَنَّك» is omitted because the meaning indicates it, i.e. 'then your eye will be gladdened.' It is not sound for «فإلينا يُرْجَعُون» to be the apodosis of both the item conjoined to and the conjoined item, because the construction «فإمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بعضَ الذين نَعِدُهم في حياتك فإلينا يُرْجَعون» is not apparent [in meaning]; but it is sound for it to be the apodosis of «أو نَتَوَفَّيَنَّك», i.e. 'then to Us they will be returned, and We will take revenge on them and punish them for not having followed you.' A parallel to this verse is His saying, Exalted is He: {فَإِمَّا نَذْهَبَنَّ بِكَ فَإِنَّا مِنْهُم مُّنتَقِمُونَ، أَوْ نُرِيَنَّكَ الذي وَعَدْنَاهُمْ فَإِنَّا عَلَيْهِمْ مُّقْتَدِرُونَ} [al-Zukhruf: 42], except that there He made the apodoses of both conditions explicit." I say: this is exactly al-Zamakhsharī's statement.
Al-Sulamī and Yaʿqūb read «يَرْجَعون» with fatḥa on the yāʾ of absence (third person), active; and Ibn Muṣarrif and Yaʿqūb also [read it] with fatḥa on the tāʾ of address.

semin-durr:78-78.t: His saying: {مِنْهُم مَّن قَصَصْنَا}: «منهم» may be a ṣifa (adjective) of «رُسُلاً», so that «مَنْ قَصَصْنا» is a fāʿil (agent) of it because it is supported [by what precedes]; and it may be a fronted khabar (predicate), with «مَنْ» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). Then there are two aspects for the clause: being a description of «رُسُلاً», which is the apparent one, and being resumptive.

semin-durr:79-79.t: His saying: {مِنْهَا، وَمِنْهَا}: The first «مِنْ» may be partitive, since not all of them are ridden; and it may be for the beginning of the extent, since what is meant by «الأنعام» is something specific, namely camels. Al-Zajjāj said: "because nothing other than them is customarily used for riding." As for the second, it is like the first. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is for clarifying the genus," and he said: "because horses are among them, and they are not eaten."

semin-durr:80-80.t: His saying: {وَعَلَى الفلك}: The word «على» was chosen here over the word «في», as in His saying {قُلْنَا احمل فِيهَا} [Hūd: 40], for congruence with His saying «وعليها»; so they answered. It appears that «في» there is more fitting, because the ship of Noah, peace be upon him, according to what is said, was closed over them, surrounding them like a container. As for other [ships], the sense of being on top is clear in them, because people are on their back.

semin-durr:81-81.t:
His saying: {فَأَيَّ آيَاتِ الله}: accusative (manṣūb) by «تُنْكِرون», and it is necessarily fronted because it has the right to the head of the speech. Makkī said: "If there were a hāʾ [pronoun] with the verb, the preferred choice would be the nominative in «أي», unlike the alif of interrogation when it enters a noun followed by a verb acting on the pronoun of the noun, where the preferred choice is the accusative, as in your saying «أزيداً ضَرَبْتُه». This is the doctrine of Sībawayh: he distinguished between the alif and «أيّ»." I say: he means that if you say «أيُّهم ضربْتَه», the preferred choice is the nominative because it does not require an implied [verb], although interrogation is present; whereas in «أزيداً ضربْتُه» the accusative is preferred on account of the interrogation, so its logical consequence would be preferring the accusative also when the interrogation is in the noun itself. The distinction is difficult. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«فأيَّ آياتِ» came according to the widespread usage. Your saying «فأيةَ آياتِ اللَّهِ» is rare, because distinguishing between masculine and feminine in nouns other than adjectives, as in «حِمار» and «حِمارة», is unusual, and in «أَيّ» it is more unusual because of its vagueness." The Shaykh said: "Among the rare instances of the feminine of «أيّ» is the saying:
3945 - بأيِّ كتابٍ أم بأيةِ سُنَّةٍ ... ترى حُبَّهم عاراً عليَّ وتَحْسَبُ
(By what scripture, or by what sunna, do you see and reckon my love for them a disgrace upon me?)
His statement 'and in «أيّ» it is more unusual': if he meant «أيّ» absolutely, it is not correct, because the widespread usage in the vocative is to make it feminine when addressing a feminine, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {ياأيتها النفس المطمئنة} [al-Fajr: 27]; and we know of no one who mentioned its masculine there, so that one would say 'يا أيُّها المرأة,' except the author of al-Badīʿ fī al-Naḥw. If he meant other than the vocative, his statement is correct: its feminine is rare in the interrogative, the relative and the conditional." I say: as for when it occurs as an adjective of an indefinite noun or as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of a definite noun, what ought to be is that both aspects are permissible, as with the relative, the feminine being rarer, as in «مررتُ بامرأةٍ أيةِ امرأة» and «جاءَتْ هندٌ أيةَ امرأةٍ». The Shaykh ought to have drawn attention to these two sub-cases.

semin-durr:82-82.t:
His saying: {فَمَآ أغنى عَنْهُم}: «ما» may be negating, or interrogative in the sense of negation, but there is no need for that.
His saying: «ما كانوا»: «ما» may be maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar), and it may be in the sense of «الذي» (that which). On the first there is no returning pronoun; on the second it is omitted, i.e. «يَكْسِبونه». It is the fāʿil (agent) of «أَغْنَى» on both assumptions.

semin-durr:83-83.t: His saying: {بِمَا عِندَهُمْ مِّنَ العلم}: There are several aspects in it. First: it is mockery of them, the meaning being: they have no knowledge. Second: it came according to their claim that they have knowledge from which they benefit. Third: «مِنْ» is in the sense of "instead of," i.e. in the worldly things they had instead of knowledge. On these aspects, both pronouns refer to the disbelievers. Fourth: both pronouns refer to the messengers, i.e. the messengers rejoiced in the knowledge they had. Fifth: the first is for the disbelievers and the second for the messengers, its meaning being: the disbelievers rejoiced with the joy of laughter and mockery at the knowledge the messengers had, since they did not accept it nor comply with the commands and prohibitions of the revelation. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Among them — i.e. the aspects — is that His saying {فَرِحُواْ بِمَا عِندَهُمْ مِّنَ العلم} is placed as an exaggeration in negating their rejoicing in the revelation, which calls for the utmost joy and delight, together with mockery of their extreme emptiness of knowledge and their ignorance." The Shaykh said: "A clause apparently affirmative is not used to express a negative clause except in a small part of speech, as in «شَرٌّ أهرَّ ذا نابٍ» ('an evil has made the fanged one snarl'), with a disagreement about it; it was permitted since its import came down to a restricted affirmation. As for the verse, it ought not to be construed on the rare usage, because that confuses the meanings of differing clauses."

semin-durr:85-85.t:
His saying: {فَلَمْ يَكُ يَنفَعُهُمْ إِيمَانُهُمْ}: «إيمانُهم» may be nominative as the noun (ism) of «كان», with «يَنْفَعُهم» a clause as a fronted khabar (predicate); and it may be nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of «يَنْفَعُهم», with the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) in «كان». This has preceded for you in detail at His saying {مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 137], and that it is not of the category of contention (tanāzuʿ), so you should consult it. The particle of negation entered upon «كان» and not upon the [verb of] benefit, because it is in the sense of "it is not sound and not fitting," as in His saying {مَا كَانَ للَّهِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ مِن وَلَدٍ} [Maryam: 35]. [Translator's note: the source reads «لا على النفي» ("not upon the negation"); the sense appears to be "not upon the benefiting (النفع)"; translated accordingly.]
His saying: «سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ»: It may be accusative as a maṣdar emphasising the content of the clause, meaning: what Allah did to them is a precedent established beforehand by Allah. It may be accusative by way of warning, i.e. "beware of Allah's way with those who deny, which has passed among His servants." «هنالك» is originally [an adverb of] place. It has been said: it is borrowed here for time; but there is no need for that, since the sense of place in it is apparent.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: {حم}: like His saying {الم} and its kind. The Two Brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī), Abū Bakr and Ibn Dhakwān read the «حاء» with pure imāla (inclination of the vowel) in the seven sūras [beginning with it]; Warsh and Abū ʿAmr read it with the intermediate imāla; and the rest with fatḥa. The majority read the «ميم» with sukūn like the rest of the disconnected letters. al-Zuhrī read the «ميم» with ḍamma, either as the predicate of an implied subject, or as a subject with what follows as the predicate. Ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿĪsā read it with fatḥa, which admits two views. One: it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "recite «حم»," and it is diptote (denied full declension) because of being a proper name and feminine, or a proper name and resembling a foreign word. That is because there is no pattern fāʿīl in Arabic patterns, unlike foreign ones such as «قابيل» and «هابيل». The second: it is a vowel of indeclinability (ḥarakat bināʾ) for lightness, like «أينَ» and «كيف». The saying of al-Kumayt admits both views:
3908 - وَجَدْنا لكم في آلِ حَمَ آيةً ... تَأَوَّلَها منا تقيٌّ ومُعْرِبُ
(We found for you in Āl Ḥā Mīm a verse; a God-fearing man and an articulate one among us interpreted it.)
and the saying of Shurayḥ ibn Awfā:
3909 - يُذَكِّرُني حمَ والرُّمْحُ شاجِرٌ ... فهلا تلا حمَ قبلَ التقدُّمِ
(He reminds me of Ḥā Mīm while the spear is locked in my body; why did he not recite Ḥā Mīm before advancing?)
Abū l-Sammāl read it with kasra. Can «حم» be pluralised as «حواميم»? Ibn al-Jawzī transmitted from his teacher al-Jawālīqī that this is an error, and that the correct thing is to say "I recited Āl Ḥā Mīm." In the ḥadīth from Ibn Masʿūd from him, peace be upon him: "When you fall upon Āl Ḥā Mīm you have fallen upon meadows." And al-Kumayt said:
3910 - وَجَدْنا لكم في آلِ حم. . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
the verse. Some of them permitted it. Ḥadīths were reported on that, among them: "The Ḥawāmīm are the brocade of the Qurʾān"; and: "Whoever wishes to graze in the lovely gardens of Paradise, let him recite the Ḥawāmīm"; and: "The likeness of the Ḥawāmīm in the Qurʾān is the likeness of the striped garments among clothes." If these ḥadīths are authentic, they are the decisive word on this.

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {تَنزِيلُ}: It is either the khabar of «حَم» if that is a mubtadaʾ, or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, or it is a mubtadaʾ itself, with the following preposition and genitive noun as its khabar.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {غَافِرِ الذنب وَقَابِلِ التوب شَدِيدِ العقاب}: There are three views on these attributes. First: that all of them are adjectives of the Majestic Name, like «العزيز العليم». It is permissible to describe a definite noun with these, even though their annexation is a lexical one (iḍāfa lafẓiyya), because it is possible to treat their annexation as semantic (iḍāfa maʿnawiyya) so that they become definite through annexation. Sībawayh stated explicitly that everything whose annexation is not pure may be made pure, and definite nouns may be described with it, except the assimilated adjective (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha). He excepted nothing else; and they are the Kufans. They say of the like of «حَسَنُ الوجهِ» that its annexation may become pure. On this, His saying «شديد العقابِ» belongs to the assimilated adjective, so how did you permit making it an adjective of a definite noun when it does not become definite by annexation?
The answer: either by adopting the school of the Kufans, namely that the annexation of the assimilated adjective may also become pure and so be definite; or by taking «شديد» in the sense of «مُشَدِّد» (one who makes severe), like «أَذِيْن» in the sense of «مُؤَذِّن», so that its annexation becomes pure.
Second: that all of them are badals (substitutes), because their annexation is not pure; al-Zamakhsharī said this. But substitution by a derived noun is very rare, unless the aspect of adjectival function is abandoned in them.
Third: that «غافر» and «قابل» are two adjectives and «شديد» a badal, for the reason given earlier, namely that the assimilated adjective does not become definite by annexation; al-Zajjāj said this. But al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-Zajjāj's making «شديد العقاب» alone a badal from the attributes has an evident awkwardness. The right way is to say: since this single indefinite was set among these definites, it signals that all of them are badals and not adjectives. An example of that is a poem all of whose tafāʿīl (metrical feet) come as «مستفعلن»: it is judged to be of the rajaz metre; but if a single foot occurs as «مَتَفاعلن», it is of the kāmil metre." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) disputed with him and said: "There is no awkwardness in that, because proceeding according to the established, sound rules is the original position. And his saying 'it signals that all of them are badals' is a non-Arabic construction, because he made «فقد آذنَتْ» the apodosis of «لَمَّا», and it is not in their speech to say «لَمَّا قام زيدٌ فقد قام عمروٌ». His saying that all of them are badals involves repetition of badals. As for the badal al-badāʾ (substitute of change of mind), for those who affirm it, repetition of badals does occur in it. But as for the badal of the whole for the whole, the part for the whole, and the badal of inclusion, there is no text from any grammarian I know of permitting or prohibiting repetition in them. However, in the words of some of our colleagues is something indicating that a badal is not repeated, namely in the poet's saying:
3911 - فإلى ابنِ أُمِّ أُناسٍ أَرْحَلُ ناقتي ... عمْروٍ فتُبْلِغُ حاجتي أو تُزْحِفُ
مَلِكٍ إذا نَزَلَ الوفودُ ببابِه ... عَرَفُوا موارِدَ مُزْبِدٍ لا يُنْزَفُ
(To the son of Umm Unās I drive my camel, to ʿAmr; she will either bring me to my need or fall short. A king at whose door, when delegations alight, they find the watering places of a foaming source that is never drained.)
He said: «مَلكٍ» is a badal from «عمرو», an indefinite badal from a definite. He said: 'If you ask: why is it not a badal from «ابن أمِّ أناسٍ»? I say: because «عمرو» was already substituted for it, so it cannot be substituted for it a second time, because it has been discarded.'" End of quotation.
The Shaykh said: "This indicates that the badal is not repeated while the badal-from is one, and it indicates that a badal from a badal is permissible." I say: he has discussed this at the end of al-Fātiḥa at His saying {غَيْرِ المغضوب عَلَيْهِم} [al-Fātiḥa: 7], so refer to it. He said: "As for his saying «تفاعيلُها», it is the plural of «تِفْعال», «تَفْعُول», «تُفْعُول» or «تَفْعيل», and none of these is counted among the parts of prosody, for its parts are limited and include none of these patterns. The correct thing was to say: 'all its parts came as «مُستفعلن»'."
al-Zamakhsharī also said: "Someone might say: they are adjectives, and the alif and lām were omitted from «شديد» only to match what precedes and follows it in wording; they have changed much of their speech from its rules for the sake of parallelism, saying «ما يعرف سحادليه مِنْ عبادليه», so they made dual what is single for the sake of what is paired. Moreover, al-Khalīl said, regarding their saying «ما يَحْسُنُ بالرجلِ مثلِك أَنْ يَفْعل ذلك» and «ما يَحْسُن بالرجلِ خيرٍ منك», that it is on the intention of the alif and lām, just as «الجَمَّاء الغفير» is on the intention of dropping the alif and lām. What made that easy is the safety from confusion and the vagueness of the described." The Shaykh said: "There is no necessity for dropping «أل» from «شديد العقاب» and likening it to a rare altered usage, namely making dual the single for the sake of the paired; the Book of Allah should be kept free of that." I say: as for parallelism (izdiwāj), which is assimilation (mushākala), as such it does occur in the Qurʾān, and you have seen several places of it.
al-Zamakhsharī also said: "It may be said that its indefiniteness and vagueness were deliberate, to indicate extreme severity and that there is nothing more dire and bitter than it, to increase the warning. And it may be said: this subtlety is what calls for choosing badal over adjective, if the way of badal is followed." End of quotation. Makkī said: "In «غافر» and «قابل», badal is permissible on the basis that they are indefinite because of referring to the future, and the adjective is permissible on the basis that they are definite because of referring to the past."
Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī said: "There is no dispute about making «غافر» and «قابل» adjectives, and they are so because they convey the meaning of continuity and permanence. «شديدُ العقابِ» likewise conveys that, because His attributes are exalted above coming into being and renewal; its meaning is that He is such that His punishment is severe. This meaning is always attained and is not described as having been attained after not being so."
The Shaykh said: "This is the speech of one who has not stood on the science of grammar and has not looked into it. It would oblige that {حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ} [al-Naml: 6] and {مَلِيكٍ مُّقْتَدِرِ} [al-Qamar: 55] be definite because His attributes are exalted above coming into being and renewal and because they are attributes that did not come about after not being; and the definiteness of His attributes with «أل» and their indefiniteness would be the same. A beginner in grammar would not say this, let alone compile in it and venture to interpret the Book of Allah the Exalted." End of quotation.
All these attributes were listed without a conjunction except «قابل التوب». Some said: "It was conjoined only because of their joint occurrence and mutual entailment and the non-separation of either from the other, and «شديد» was cut off from them, not conjoined, because of its being on its own." The Shaykh said: "In this is a Muʿtazilite tendency. The school of the People of the Sunna is that forgiving the sinner is permissible even if he has not repented, except for shirk." I say: how far this is from the Muʿtazilite tendency! Then I say: the mutual entailment is necessary in that, whenever the Exalted accepts repentance, He has forgiven the sin, and that suffices for mutual entailment.
al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the point of the «واو» in His saying «وقابلِ التَّوْبِ»? I say: in it is a great subtlety: it conveys that for the repentant sinner two mercies are combined: that He accepts his repentance and records it as one of the acts of obedience, and that He makes it an eraser of sins, as if he had not sinned; as if He had said: the combiner of forgiveness and acceptance." End of quotation.
After this elegant statement and the bringing out of these fine meanings, the Shaykh said: "How great is this man's bragging and his rhetorical flourish! What he conveyed is that the «واو» is for combining, and this is well known from the surface of the science of grammar." I say: someone recited to me:
3912 - وكم مِنْ عائبٍ قَوْلاً صحيحاً ... وآفَتُه من الفَهْمِ السَّقيمِ
(How many a one faults a sound statement, while his affliction is a sick understanding.)
and another said:
3913 - قد تُنْكِرُ العينُ ضوءَ الشمسِ مِنْ رَمَدٍ ... ويُنكِرُ الفَمُ طَعْمَ الماءِ مِنْ سَقَمِ
(The eye may deny the light of the sun from ophthalmia, and the mouth may deny the taste of water from sickness.)
«التَّوْبُ» may be a singular noun meant as a genus, like «الذَّنْب», or it may be a plural of «تَوْبة», like «تَمْر» and «تَمْرَة». «ذي الطَّوْلِ» is an adjective or a badal as already mentioned. «الطَّوْلُ» is abundance of bounty.
{لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ} may be resumptive, or a ḥāl, and it is an inseparable ḥāl. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It may be an adjective." On this, its apparent sense is invalid, since a clause is not an adjective of definite nouns. It is possible that he means it is an adjective of «شديد العقاب», because it did not become definite for him by annexation. The same is said of «إليه المصيرُ» as of the clause before it, and it may be a ḥāl from the clause before it.

semin-durr:4-4.t: The majority read «فلا يَغْرُرْكَ» unassimilated (with the two rās separate), which is the dialect of the Ḥijāz. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read «فلا يَغُرَّكَ» assimilated, with fatḥa on the rāʾ, which is the dialect of Tamīm.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «برَسولها», returning the pronoun to the wording of «أُمَّة»; the majority return it to its meaning. In His saying «ليَأْخُذوه» is an expression of the effect through its cause; that is, killing is an effect of seizing, and from it the captive is called «أَخِيْذ». He said:
3914 - فإمَّا تَأْخُذُوني تَقْتُلوني ... فكَمْ مِنْ آخِذٍ يَهْوَى خُلودي
(If you take me, you will kill me; but how many a taker wishes for my immortality.)
In His saying «عِقابِ» the kasra suffices in place of the yā' of the first person, in continuation and in pause, because it is at the head of a verse-ending (fāṣila).

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {وَكَذَلِكَ}: The «كاف» may be in the position of nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and the matter is thus," and then He reports that the Word of Allah has become due against them in the form of punishment; or it may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "in the like of that obligation of their punishment, it became obligatory upon the disbelievers."
His saying «أنهم أصحابُ»: it may be with the preposition omitted, i.e. «لأنَّهم», in which case the two usual views apply to its position. It may also be in the position of nominative as a badal from «كلمةُ». The disagreement of the readers on the singular and plural of «كلمة» has already preceded.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {الذين يَحْمِلُونَ}: mubtadaʾ, with «ويُسَبِّحون» as its khabar.
The majority read the ʿayn of «العَرْش» with fatḥa. Ibn ʿAbbās and others read it with ḍamma; it was said that it may be a plural of «عَرْش», like «سُقْف» in «سَقْف».
His saying «ومَنْ حَوْلَه» may be in the position of nominative, conjoined to «الذين يَحْملون», reporting of both groups that they glorify, and this is the apparent view; or in the position of accusative, conjoined to «العرش», meaning they also carry the angels who encircle the Throne. That is not apparent.
His saying: «رَبَّنا» is the object of an implied saying, the implied form being "They say: Our Lord." The implied saying is in the position of accusative as ḥāl from the agent of «يَسْتَغْفرون», or a khabar after a khabar. «رحمةً وعِلْماً» is a tamyīz (specification) transferred from agency, i.e. "Your mercy and Your knowledge encompass all things."

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ التي وَعَدْتَّهُمْ}: A parallel has preceded in Maryam. The majority read «جناتِ» in the plural; al-Aʿmash and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «جنة» in the singular.
His saying «ومَنْ صَلَحَ» is in the position of accusative, either conjoined to the object of «أدْخِلْهُمْ» or to the object of «وَعَدْتَهم». al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj said: "Its accusative is from two places: if you wish, from the pronoun in «أَدْخِلْهم», and if you wish, from the pronoun in «وَعَدْتَهم»."
The majority read the lām of «صَلَح» with fatḥa; one says «صَلُح فهو صالحٌ». Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with ḍamma; one says «صَلَح فهو صَليح». The majority read «ذُرِّيَّاتهم» in the plural; ʿĪsā read «وذُرِّيَّتهم» in the singular.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ}: The tanwīn is a compensation for an omitted clause; but there is no clause explicitly stated in the speech for which this tanwīn is a compensation, unlike His saying {وَأَنتُمْ حِينَئِذٍ تَنظُرُونَ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 84], i.e. "when it reaches the throat," because of its earlier mention in the wording. So a clause must be implied for which this is the compensation; the implied form is "the day when he is called to account for them."

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {إِذْ تُدْعَوْنَ}: It is accusative by an implied [operator], which this apparent wording indicates, the implied form being "your being detested, when you were called." Some implied "Remember when you were called." al-Zamakhsharī allowed that it be accusative by the first «المَقْت». The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) objected to him: it would entail separation between the maṣdar and its object by a foreigner, namely the predicate. He said: "This is among the obvious points of grammar that hardly escape a beginner, let alone one who is claimed by the non-Arabs to be the shaykh of the Arabs and non-Arabs." I say: the like of this does not escape Abū l-Qāsim; he only meant that it indicates its governor, and on such an implication it is a Kufan school view that he adopted, or because the adverbial admits a latitude that others do not. What obscurity is there in this that he should be attacked in this manner? How well one has said:
3915 - حَسَدُوا الفتى إذ لم يَنالُوا سَعْيَه ... فالقومُ أعداءٌ له وخُصومُ
كضَرائرِ الحَسْناءِ قُلْنَ لِوَجْهها ... كَذِباً وزُوْراً إنه لدَمِيمُ
(They envied the youth because they could not attain his striving, so the people are his enemies and adversaries; like the co-wives of a beautiful woman who said to her face, falsely and untruly, that it is ugly.)
This objection was preceded by Abū l-Baqāʾ, who said: "«مَقْتُ الله» cannot govern it because it is a maṣdar of which a report has been made, namely His saying «أكبرُ»." From there the Shaykh took it. It cannot be accusative by the second «المقت» either, because they did not detest themselves at the time of their being called to faith; they detested themselves only on the Day of Resurrection. The apparent view is that Allah's detestation occurs in this world. al-Ḥasan allowed that it be in the Hereafter. The Shaykh weakened this, saying that «إذْ تُدْعَوْن» would then remain "loose" from the speech, having no preceding operator and nothing to interpret an operator. But if the detestation is in this world, an operator may be implied for it, the implied form being «مَقْتِكم». I say: this boldness against the like of al-Ḥasan makes light for you his boldness against al-Zamakhsharī and the like.
The lām in «لَمَقْتُ» is the lām of inception or of oath. Its object is omitted, i.e. "Allah's detestation of you" or "of yourselves"; it is a maṣdar annexed to its agent like the second one. It is not permissible that the question be a case of conflict of operators (tanāzuʿ) over «أنفسَكم» between the two detestations, so as not to entail separation by the predicate between the first detestation and its object, on the assumption that it is the operating one. But the grammarians differ on a question: conflict in the two verbs of wonder. Whoever forbids it argues with what I mentioned, because verbs of wonder are not separated from their objects. Whoever allows it says one must adhere to the second operating, so that separation is not entailed. Let this be of that kind. The truth is that it is not permissible, since it contradicts the rule of tanāzuʿ.

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {وَحْدَهُ}: Two views. One: it is a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl, and it is permissible for it to be definite in wording because it is equivalent to an indefinite, as though it were said "alone." The second, which is the view of Yūnus: it is accusative as an adverbial, the implied form being "he was called on his own," and it is a maṣdar with its additions dropped, the original being «أَوْحَدْتُه إيحاداً».

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {رَفِيعُ}: Two views. One: it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is «ذو العرشِ», and «يُلْقي الروحَ» may be a second khabar, or a ḥāl; or all three may be khabars of an omitted mubtadaʾ; or all three may be khabars of His saying {هُوَ الذي يُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ}. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Three khabars which may follow in sequence on His saying {هُوَ الذي يُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ}, or be khabars of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and they differ in definiteness and indefiniteness." I say: as for the first, there is a long separation and a multiplicity of khabars that are not in the sense of a single khabar. As for the second, it has a multiplicity of khabars not in the sense of a single khabar, and this is a disputed question. It is not permissible that «ذو العرش» be an adjective of «رفيعُ الدرجاتِ» if we make it an assimilated adjective; but if we make it an intensive form (mithāl mubālagha), i.e. "He raises the degrees of the believers," it is permissible provided that its annexation is made pure, and likewise according to those who permit the annexation of the assimilated adjective to be pure, as already mentioned.
«رفيعَ» was read in the accusative for praise. «مِنْ أَمْرِه» is attached to «يُلْقِي», and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the range. It may be attached to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl from «الروح».
His saying: «لِيُنْذِرَ»: the majority read it in the active, with «اليوم» in the accusative. The agent is Allah the Exalted, or the Spirit, or whomever He wills, or the Messenger. The accusative of «اليوم» is either adverbial, with the thing warned about omitted, the implied form being "to warn of the punishment on the Day of Meeting," or a direct object by extension in the adverbial.
Ubayy and a group read it likewise, except that he made «اليوم» nominative as figurative agent, i.e. "that the Day of Meeting may warn the people of punishment." al-Ḥasan and al-Yamānī read «لِتُنْذِرَ» with tā' above. Two views: first, that the agent is the pronoun of the addressee, who is the Messenger ﷺ; second, that the agent is the pronoun of the Spirit, which is feminine according to one view. al-Yamānī also read «لِيُنْذَرَ» in the passive, with «يومُ» in the nominative, which supports its accusative in the majority reading as a direct object by extension.
The yā' of «التلاقي» was retained in continuation and pause by Ibn Kathīr; Warsh retained it in pause but not in continuation, without disagreement; the others dropped it in continuation and pause, except Qālūn, from whom two ways were reported: one like Warsh, one like the others. The same disagreement applies exactly to {يَوْمَ التناد} [Ghāfir: 32]. The justification of these two ways has preceded in al-Raʿd at His saying {الكبير المتعال} [al-Raʿd: 9].

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ هُم بَارِزُونَ}: There are four views on «يوم». One: it is a badal from «يوم التلاق», a total substitute (badal kull min kull). Two: it is accusative by «التلاق», i.e. the meeting takes place on the day of their emerging. Three: it is accusative by His saying {لاَ يخفى عَلَى الله}; Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned it. This depends on one of three views regarding «لا»: whether what follows it operates on what precedes it. The third is the distinction: if it falls as the answer to an oath it is prevented, otherwise it is permitted. So this is allowed under two of these views. Four: it is accusative by an implied "Remember". «يومَ» is a future adverbial like «إذا». Sībawayh does not see the annexation of a future adverbial to nominal clauses, while al-Akhfash does; for this reason Sībawayh implied a verb before the noun in His saying {إِذَا السمآء انشقت} [al-Inshiqāq: 1] and the like, whereas al-Akhfash did not imply it. On this, the apparent sense of the verse is with al-Akhfash. Sībawayh is answered: «هم» is not a mubtadaʾ but nominative by an omitted verb interpreted by the active participle, i.e. "on the day they emerged," and «بارِزون» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ; when the verb was omitted the pronoun became detached and remained as you see. This is as they said regarding the saying:
3916 - لو بغيرِ الماءِ حَلْقي شَرِقٌ ... كُنْتُ كالغَصَّانِ بالماءِ اعتصاري
(Had my throat choked on something other than water, I would have been like the one choking, taking refuge in water.)
in that «حَلْقي» is nominative by a verb that «شَرِقٌ» interprets, because only verbs follow «لو»; and likewise the saying:
3917 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فهَلاَّ نَفْسُ لَيْلى شَفيعُها
because only verbs follow «هَلاَّ». So the interpreted items in these places are nouns preceded [by verbs]; and it is parallel to «أنا زيداً ضاربُه» in regard to interpretation. The vowel of «يومَ هم» is a vowel of declension (iʿrāb) on the well-known view. Some permit the adverbial to be indeclinable even if annexed to an imperfect verb or a nominal clause, and they are the Kufans. Some have erred and made it obligatory for an adverbial annexed to nominal clauses to be indeclinable. You know from what preceded that, for the Basrans, only what is annexed to a past verb is indeclinable, as in the saying:
3918 - على حينَ عاتَبْتَ المشيبَ على الصِّبا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
the verse. This was dealt with in full at the end of al-Māʾida. They wrote «يومَ هم» here and in al-Dhāriyāt separated, which is the original.
His saying: «لا يَخْفَى»: it may be resumptive, or a ḥāl from the pronoun of «بارِزون», or a second khabar.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {اليوم}: an adverbial for His saying «لِمَن المُلْكُ», and it may be an adverbial for the preposition-and-genitive after it, since the implied form is «المُلْكُ لله», which is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. «اليومَ» is governed by «تُجْزَى», and the last «اليومَ» is the khabar of «لا ظلمَ».

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ الأزفة}: it may be a direct object by extension, or an adverbial with the object omitted. «الآزِفَةُ» is the near one, from «أَزِفَ الشيءُ», i.e. it drew near. al-Nābigha said:
3919 - أَزِف التَّرَحُّلُ غيرَ أنَّ رِكابَنا ... لَمَّا تَزَلْ برِحالِنا وكأنْ قَدِ
(Departure has drawn near, except that our riding camels have not yet left with our saddles, and it is as if they already had.)
and Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr said:
3920 - بان الشبابُ وهذا الشيبُ قد أَزِفا ... ولا أرَى لشبابٍ بائنٍ خلفا
(Youth has departed and this grey hair has drawn near, and I see no replacement for departed youth.)
al-Rāghib said: "«أَزِفَ» and «أَفِدَ» are close, but «أَزِفَ» is said with regard to the narrowness of its time. One says «أزِفَ الشُّخوصُ». «الأَزَفُ» is the narrowness of time." I say: he made a difference between them, and the verse of al-Nābigha is also reported as «أَفِدَ الترحُّلُ». «الآزِفَةُ» is an adjective of an omitted noun, so the implied form may be «الساعة الآزِفَةُ» or «الطامَّةُ الآزِفة».
His saying: «إذ القلوبُ» is a badal from «يومِ الآزِفةِ», or from «هم» in «أَنْذِرْهُمْ», a badal of inclusion.
His saying: «كاظِمين» is accusative as ḥāl. They differed over its owner and its operator. al-Ḥawfī said: "«القلوبُ» is a mubtadaʾ, «لدى الحناجِر» is its khabar, and «كاظمين» is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in it." I say: an answer is needed for the plural of «القلوب» in the plural of rational beings: when what is attributed to rational beings was attributed to them, they were pluralised as they are, like His saying {رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ} [Yūsuf: 4], {فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 4]. Second: it is a ḥāl from «القلوب». The same question and answer as before apply. Third: it is a ḥāl from the owners of the hearts. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a ḥāl from the owners of the hearts in meaning, since the meaning is: 'when their hearts are at the throats, they suppressing [grief] over them.'" I say: it is as though he made «أل» a compensation for the pronoun in «حناجرهم». Fourth: it is a ḥāl from «هم» in «أَنْذِرْهم», and an anticipated ḥāl, because at the time of the warning they are not suppressing.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«كاظِمين» is a ḥāl from what «إذ القلوب» is a badal from, or from what «القلوب» is annexed to, since the meaning is 'when the hearts of the people are at their throats', like His saying {تَشْخَصُ فِيهِ الأبصار} [Ibrāhīm: 42], he meant 'in which their eyes stare'." I say: the apparent sense of his statement is that it is a ḥāl from what it is a badal from.
His saying «إذ القلوبُ» is problematic, because it was made a badal from His saying «يومَ الآزِفَة», and this is not valid at all. What he means is the second view: that it is a badal of inclusion from «هم» in «أَنْذِرْهُمْ», and then it is valid. The discussion of «الكَظْم» and «الحناجر» has already preceded in Āl ʿImrān and al-Aḥzāb.
His saying: {وَلاَ شَفِيعٍ يُطَاعُ}: «يُطاعُ» may be judged in its position as genitive, an adjective by wording, or nominative, an adjective by position, because it is conjoined to what is made genitive by the redundant «مِنْ».
His saying {وَلاَ شَفِيعٍ يُطَاعُ} belongs to the type of:
3921 - على لاحِبٍ لا يُهْتَدى بمَنارِه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(On a clear road that is not guided by its landmark...)
i.e. there is no intercessor, so no obedience; or there is an intercessor but he is not obeyed.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {يَعْلَمُ}: Four views. One, the apparent one: it is another khabar of «هو» in His saying {هُوَ الذي يُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ}. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: to what is His saying {يَعْلَمُ خَآئِنَةَ الأعين} connected? I say: it is one of the khabars of «هو» in His saying {هُوَ الذي يُرِيكُمْ}, like {يُلْقِي الروح مِنْ أَمْرِهِ} [Ghāfir: 15]; but «يُلْقي الروحَ» was given a reason by His saying «لِيُنْذِرَ», and then he digressed to mention the states of the Day of Meeting up to His saying {وَلاَ شَفِيعٍ يُطَاعُ}, so for that reason it is distant from its sisters."
Second: it is connected to His saying «وأَنْذِرْهم»: when he was commanded to warn them of the Day of the Imminent and the intensity of grief and distress that befalls in it, and that the wrongdoer finds none to protect him and no intercessor for him, He mentioned His awareness of everything that issues from creation, in secret and in the open. On this, this clause has no position, because it is equivalent to a reason for the command to warn.
Third: it is connected to His saying {سَرِيعُ الحساب} [Ghāfir: 17].
Fourth: it is connected to His saying {لاَ يخفى عَلَى الله مِنْهُمْ شَيْءٌ} [Ghāfir: 16]. On these last two views it may run in the course of a reason, or be in the position of accusative as ḥāl.
«خائنةُ الأَعْيُن»: two views. One: it is a maṣdar like «العافية», i.e. "He knows the treachery of the eyes." Two: it is an adjective in its usual sense, belonging to the annexation of the adjective to the described, the original being «الأعين الخائنة», like the saying:
3922 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وإن سَقَيْتِ كِرامَ الناسِ فاسْقِينا
(...and if you give drink to the noble among people, give us drink.)
al-Zamakhsharī rejected it and said: "It is not good to mean 'the treacherous of the eyes,' since His saying {وَمَا تُخْفِي الصدور} does not support it," meaning that it is not fitting that a meaning be paralleled by anything but a meaning. There is some question about this, since someone might say: we do not grant that «ما» in {وَمَا تُخْفِي الصدور} is a maṣdar particle such that what he said follows; rather it may be in the sense of «الذي» (that which), which is an expression of that hidden thing itself, so it parallels a non-maṣdar noun with its like.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {والذين يَدْعُونَ}: Nāfiʿ and Hishām read «تَدْعُون» in the second person, addressing the polytheists; the others read it in the third person, reporting of them.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {فَيَنظُرُواْ}: it may be accusative as the answer to the question, or jussive, conjoined to what precedes it, like the saying:
3923 - ألم تَسْأَلْ فتُخْبِرْكَ الرُّسومُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Did you not ask, so that the traces inform you...)
Some transmitted it with both the jussive and the accusative.
His saying: «منهم قوةً»: Ibn ʿĀmir read «منكم» by way of shift (iltifāt); the others read the pronoun of the third person in line with the preceding third-person pronouns.
His saying: «وآثاراً» is conjoined to «قوةً», and it is equivalent to His saying {يَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الجبال بُيُوتاً آمِنِينَ} [al-Ḥijr: 82]. al-Zamakhsharī made it accusative by an implied [verb], saying: "Or he meant: 'and greater in traces,' like the saying:
3924 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . قد غدا ... مُتَقَلِّداً سَيْفاً ورُمْحا
(...he has set out, wearing a sword and [carrying] a spear)
meaning: and bearing a spear." There is no need for this, as it can be dispensed with.

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {أَوْ أَن}: The Kufans read «أو أَنْ» with «أو», which is for vagueness (ibhām), and the others with the conjunctive «واو», in the sense of the combination of the two events: the change [of religion] and the appearance of corruption together. Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ read «يُظْهِرَ» with ḍamma on the yā' and kasra on the hā', from «أظهر», its agent being the pronoun of Mūsā, peace be upon him, with «الفسادَ» in the accusative as direct object. The others read it with fatḥa on the yā' and the hā', from «ظهر», with «الفسادُ» nominative as agent. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يُظْهَرَ» in the passive, with «الفسادُ» nominative because it stands in place of the agent. Mujāhid read «يَظَّهَّرَ» with shadda on the ẓāʾ and the hā'; its original is «يَتَظَهَّر», from «تَظَهَّر» with shadda on the hā', so the tā' was assimilated into the ẓāʾ. «الفسادُ» is nominative as agent. Ibn Kathīr opened the yā' of {ذروني أَقْتُلْ موسى}, and the others left it with sukūn.

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {عُذْتُ}: Abū ʿAmr and the Two Brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) assimilated, and they pronounced the dhāl clearly with the tā'; the others only pronounce it clearly. «لا يُؤْمِنُ» is an adjective of «متكبِّر».

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ}: It may be attached to the following «يَكْتُمُ», i.e. "he conceals it from the family of Pharaoh". Second, and it is the apparent one: it is attached to an omitted [word] as an adjective of «رجل». It came here in the finest order: He put first the single word, then what is close to it, namely the preposition, then the clause. The clarification of this question has already preceded in al-Māʾida and elsewhere. Resulting from the two views: was this man a relative of Pharaoh? On the first there is no indication in it; on the second there is. Some have rejected the first view: one does not say «كَتَمْتُ مِنْ فلانٍ كذا», but «كَتَمْتُ فلاناً كذا», so it takes two objects directly. The Exalted said {وَلاَ يَكْتُمُونَ الله حَدِيثاً} [al-Nisāʾ: 42]. The poet said:
3925 - كَتَمْتُكَ هَمَّاً بالجَمومَيْنِ ساهِراً ... وهَمَّيْن هَمَّاً مُسْتَكِنَّاً وظاهراً
أحاديثَ نَفْسٍ تشتكي ما برَبِّها ... ووِرْدَ هُمومٍ لَنْ يَجِدْنَ مَصادِرا
(I concealed from you a worry, sleepless at al-Jamūmayn, and two worries: one hidden and one apparent; the talk of a soul complaining of what ails it, and a coming of cares that find no way out.)
i.e. "I concealed from you the talk of a soul and two worries", so he put the conjoined before what it is conjoined to; its place is poetry.
His saying: {أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّيَ}: i.e. "out of dislike that he should say" or "because he says." The majority read the ʿayn of «رَجُل» with ḍamma, which is the most eloquent; al-Aʿmash and ʿAbd al-Wārith read it with sukūn, which is the dialect of Tamīm and Najd. al-Zamakhsharī said: "You may imply an omitted muḍāf, i.e. 'the time that he says'. The meaning: 'Do you kill him the moment you hear this saying from him, without deliberation or thought?'" The Shaykh rejected what he allowed: implying this "time" is not permissible except with an explicitly stated maṣdar. You say «جِئْتُكَ صياحَ الدِّيْكِ», i.e. at the time of its crowing; but if you said «أجيْئُك أنْ صاحَ الديكُ» or «أَنْ يصيحَ», it would not be valid. The grammarians stated this explicitly.
His saying: «وقد جاءَكم» is a circumstantial clause, which may be from the object. If it is said it is indefinite, the answer is that it is in the sphere of the interrogative, and everything that justifies beginning with an indefinite justifies a ḥāl from it. It may also be a ḥāl from the agent.
His saying: {بَعْضُ الذي يَعِدُكُمْ}: «بعض» is in its usual sense. He said that only to make light of Mūsā's, peace be upon him, due in part in the outward speech, to show them that it was not the speech of someone who gave him his full due, let alone one who takes his side. al-Zamakhsharī said this. This is better than the saying of others that it means "all", and they recited the saying of Labīd:
3926 - تَرَّاكُ أَمْكنةٍ إذا لم يَرْضَها ... أو يَرْتَبِطْ بعضُ النفوسِ حِمامُها
(A leaver of places if he does not like them, or if some souls are tied to their fate [of death].)
and they recited the saying of ʿAmr ibn Shuyaym:
3927 - قد يُدْرِكُ المتأنِّي بعضَ حاجتِه ... وقد يكونُ مع المستعجِلِ الزَّلَلُ
(The deliberate man may attain some of his need, while the hasty man may be accompanied by error.)
and the saying of another:
3928 - إنَّ الأمورَ إذا الأحداثُ دَبَّرها ... دون الشيوخِ ترى في بعضِها خَلَلا
(When youths manage affairs without the elders, you see in some of them a defect.)
I do not know how they understood "all" from the last two verses. As for the first, there is some evidence, because death comes upon all. When al-Zamakhsharī related this from Abū ʿUbayda and recited from him the verse of Labīd, he said: "If the transmission from him is sound, then al-Māzinī's saying about the question of «عَلْقى» is deserved in his case: 'He was too coarse to understand what I say to him.'"
I say: al-Māzinī's question with him was that Abū ʿUbayda said to al-Māzinī: "How the grammarians lie! They say that the hāʾ of the feminine does not enter upon the alif of the feminine, and that the alif in «عَلْقَى» is one of annexation (alif al-ilḥāq). He said: I said to him: what do you object to in that? He said: I heard Ruʾba recite:
3929 - يَنْحَطُّ في عَلْقَى وفي مُكُوْرِ
(He descends among the «عَلْقَى» and the «مُكُور».)
and he did not give it tanwīn. I said: what is the singular of «عَلْقى»? He said: «عَلْقاةٌ». al-Māzinī said: I held back and did not explain to him, because he was too coarse to understand the like of this." I say: al-Māzinī found him coarse only because the alif of annexation takes the tā' of the feminine, indicating singularity, so one says «أَرْطى» and «أَرْطاة»; what is prevented is its entry upon the alif of the feminine, like «دَعْوى» and «صَرْعى». As for the lack of tanwīn on «عَلْقَى», it is because he made it the name of a specific thing [and the shortened alif of annexation, when the noun is a proper name, runs like the tā' of the feminine, so the noun it is in is diptote, as «فاطمة» is; and «قائمة» is declined]. [Translator's note: the bracketed passage at the end appears in the source as an editorial addition in square brackets.]

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {ظَاهِرِينَ}: a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لكم», and the operator in it and in «اليومَ» is what «لكم» is attached to.
His saying: «ما أُرِيْكُمْ»: it is from the seeing of belief, so it takes two objects, the second being {إِلاَّ مَآ أرى}.
His saying: «الرَّشادِ»: the majority read it with the shīn lightened, a maṣdar of «رشَدَ يَرْشُدُ». Muʿādh ibn Jabal read it with the shīn doubled; Abū l-Fatḥ and others parsed it as an intensive adjective, like «ضَرَب فهو ضرَّاب». al-Naḥḥās said: "It is a solecism, and he imagined it from the quadriliteral," meaning «أَرْشد». al-Naḥḥās was answered that it may be from the triliteral «رَشَدَ», which is the apparent view. The form faʿʿāl has also come from af ʿala, although it is not regular. They said: «أَدْرَك فهو دَرَّاك», «أَجْبَرَ فهو جَبَّار», «أَقْصَر فهو قَصَّار», «أَسْأَر فهو سَآَّر». What shows that it is an intensive adjective is that Muʿādh used to explain it as the way of Allah.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "I find it unlikely of Muʿādh, may Allah be pleased with him; did Pharaoh claim anything other than divinity? And the construction of the wording on this composition is unsettled." I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya means: how could Pharaoh say that, acknowledging that there is someone other than himself who guides to right guidance, while he claims to be a god? But what Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn Jubāra, the author of al-Kāmil, ascribed to Muʿādh ibn Jabal of the stated reading is not in the «الرشاد» which is in Pharaoh's speech, as they imagined, but in the second «الرشاد» which is from the believer's speech afterwards. This is indicated by what Abū l-Faḍl al-Rāzī said in his book al-Lawāmiḥ: "Muʿādh ibn Jabal: «سبيل الرشاد», the second word with shadda, and likewise al-Ḥasan; and it is the way of Allah the Exalted which He made clear to His servants. Muʿādh explained it so. It is transferred from «مُرْشِد», like «دَرَّاك» from «مُدْرِك», «جَبَّار» from «مُجْبر», and «قَصَّار» from «مُقْصِر» concerning the matter, and there are a few parallels. As for «قَصَّار الثوب» it is from «قَصَر الثوبَ قِصارةً»." On this, Ibn ʿAṭiyya's earlier difficulty disappears, and the reading and interpretation become clear.
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is one from whom guidance or right conduct is abundant," meaning that it may be from the quadriliteral «أرشدَ» or the triliteral «رَشَد». The better is that it be from the triliteral, as you know that it is regular, unlike the first.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {مِثْلَ دَأْبِ}: «مثل» may be a badal, or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ التناد}: The disagreement over its yā' has already preceded: how it is dropped and kept. It is the maṣdar of «تَنادَى», like «تقاتَلَ تقاتُلاً». The original is «تَنادُياً» with ḍamma on the dāl, but they put kasra to keep the yā' sound. A group read the dāl with sukūn, treating continuation like pause. «تنادَى القومُ» means some of them called to others. He said:
3930 - تنادَوْا فقالوا أَرْدَتِ الخيلُ فارساً ... فقُلْنا: عُبَيْدُ الله ذلكمُ الرَّدِي
(They called to one another and said: the horses have destroyed a horseman; we said: ʿUbayd Allāh, he is the one destroyed.)
and another said:
3931 - تنادَوْا بالرحيلِ غَداً ... وفي تَرْحالِهم نَفْسي
(They called to one another to depart tomorrow, and my soul is in their departing.)
Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Kalbī, Abū Ṣāliḥ, Ibn Miqsam and al-Zaʿfarānī, among others, read it with shadda, as a maṣdar of «تَنادَّ», from «نَدَّ البعيرُ» when the camel fled and bolted. It has the meaning of His saying {يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ المرء مِنْ أَخِيهِ} [ʿAbasa: 34] and the rest. In the ḥadīth: "The people will have a rout in which they flee, thinking they will find a place of escape." Umayya ibn Abī l-Ṣalt said:
3932 - وبَثَّ الخَلْقَ فيها إذ دَحاها ... فهُمْ سُكَّانُها حتى التنادي
(He spread creation in it when He spread it out, so they are its inhabitants until the Day of Calling.)

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ}: it may be a badal from «يوم التَّناد», or accusative by an implied "I mean". It cannot be an ʿaṭf bayān, because it is indefinite and what precedes is definite. It has already preceded for you, at His saying {فِيهِ آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ مَّقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 97], that al-Zamakhsharī made it an explication despite their difference in definiteness and indefiniteness, which is the reverse of our case, for in our case the second is indefinite and the first definite.
His saying: {مَا لَكُمْ مِّنَ الله مِنْ عَاصِمٍ}: «مِنْ عاصِمٍ» may be an agent of the preposition-and-genitive, relying on a negation, or a mubtadaʾ, with «مِنْ» redundant under both assumptions. «من الله» is attached to «عاصِم».

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {حتى إِذَا}: a limit for His saying «فما زِلْتُمْ». It was read {ألَن يَبْعَثَ الله} with the hamza of affirmation, they affirming to one another.
His saying: «كذلك»: i.e. "the matter is thus." «ويُضِلُّ الله» is resumptive, or an adjective of a maṣdar, i.e. "like Allah's leading you astray, when they did not accept from Yūsuf, peace be upon him, Allah leads astray whoever is a transgressor."

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {الذين يُجَادِلُونَ}: Ten views are possible. One: it is a badal from His saying {مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ}, pluralised in consideration of the meaning of «مَنْ». Two: it is an explication of it. Three: it is an adjective of it, also pluralised according to the meaning of «مَنْ». Four: it is accusative by an implied "I mean". Five: it is nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who". Six: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «يَطْبَعُ اللَّهُ» as its khabar, and «كذلك» the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ too, i.e. "the matter is thus", and the pronoun returning from the clause «يَطْبَعُ» to the mubtadaʾ is omitted, i.e. "on every arrogant heart of theirs". Seven: it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is «كَبُرَ مَقْتاً», but a muḍāf must be omitted so that the pronoun in «كَبُرَ» returns to it. The implied form is: "the state of those who dispute is great in detestation," with «مَقْتاً» a tamyīz transferred from agency, the implied form being "the detestation of their state, i.e. the state of the disputers, has become great." Eight: «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ also, but no muḍāf is implied, and the agent of «كَبُرَ» is a pronoun returning to their dispute, understood from His saying «ما يُجادِلُ». The implied form is: "their dispute has become great in detestation," and «مَقْتاً» as before, i.e. "the detestation of their dispute has become great." Nine: «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ also, and the khabar is {بِغَيْرِ سُلْطَانٍ أَتَاهُمْ}. al-Zamakhsharī said this. The Shaykh rejected it: it dissociates the speech from itself, because the apparent view is that «بغير سُلْطان» is attached to «يُجادلون», and it cannot be conceived as a khabar for «الذين» because it is a preposition-and-genitive, so the implied form would be "those who dispute are or abide in the absence of authority," i.e. "in the absence of authority," since the «باء» would then be locative, a predicate about bodies. Ten: it is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is omitted, i.e. "obstinate" or the like; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this.
His saying: «كَبُرَ مَقْتاً» may be meant as wonder and exaggeration, or as censure, like «بِئْس». That is because the pattern faʿula with ḍamma on the ʿayn may be built from what may be wondered at, and runs in the course of «نِعْم» and «بئس» in all rulings. As to its agent, six views. First: it is a pronoun returning to the state, muḍāf to «الذين», as explained earlier. Second: it is a pronoun returning to their dispute, understood from «يُجادلون», as also explained. Third: it is the «كاف» in «كذلك». al-Zamakhsharī said: "The agent of «كَبُرَ» is His saying «كذلك», i.e. 'the like of that dispute has become great in detestation', and «ويَطْبع اللَّهُ» is a resumptive speech." The Shaykh rejected it: it dissociates the speech and adopts an unsound school. As for the dissociation, what appears in the Qurʾān as «كذلك نَطْبَعُ» or «يَطْبع» occurs only linked to one another, so likewise this. As for adopting an unsound school, he made the «كاف» a noun, and it is a noun only in necessity, contrary to al-Akhfash.
Fourth: the agent is omitted; al-Zamakhsharī transmitted it. He said: "Whoever said «كَبُرَ مَقْتاً عند الله جِدالُهم» has omitted the agent, and the agent cannot be omitted." I say: the one who said that is al-Ḥawfī, but he did not mean thereby to explain the iʿrāb; he meant to explain the meaning, which is the meaning of what I said before, that the agent is a pronoun returning to their dispute understood from its verb. al-Ḥawfī stated the original, which is the overt noun, and what he meant is a pronoun returning to it.
Fifth: the agent is a pronoun returning to what follows it, the tamyīz, like «نِعْمَ رَجُلاً زيدٌ» and «بئس غلاماً عمروٌ». Sixth: it is a pronoun returning to «مَنْ» in His saying {مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ}. He returned the pronoun of «كَبُرَ» in the singular by the wording of it; then he has observed the wording of «مَنْ» first in {مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ كَذَّابٌ}, then its meaning second in His saying {الذين يُجَادِلُونَ} to the end, then its wording third in His saying «كَبُر». All this if you parse «الذين» as following «مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌ» as an adjective, explication or badal.
You know that the clause «كَبُرَ مَقْتاً» has two views. One: nominative, if we make it a khabar of a mubtadaʾ. Second: it has no position, if you do not make it a khabar but a resumptive clause. His saying «عندَ الله» is attached to «كَبُرَ»; and it was mentioned that it may also be a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or an agent, and both are weak. Third, and it is the sound one: it is governed by «يَطْبَعُ», i.e. "like that sealing, Allah seals." As for «يطبعُ اللَّهُ», two views, the clearer being that it is resumptive; the second, that it is the khabar of the relative, as all this was explained earlier.
His saying: «قَلْبِ متكبِّرٍ»: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Dhakwān read «قلب» with tanwīn, describing the heart with arrogance and tyranny, because both arise from it, even if the whole [person] is meant, as it is described with sin in His saying {فَإِنَّهُ آثِمٌ قَلْبُهُ} [al-Baqara: 283]. The others read «قلب» annexed to what follows, i.e. "on every heart of an arrogant person." al-Zamakhsharī implied a muḍāf in the first reading, i.e. "on every possessor of an arrogant heart", making the attribute belong to the owner of the heart. The Shaykh said: "There is no necessity calling for believing in the omission." I say: rather there is a necessity for it, namely the agreement of the two readings, since the described then becomes the same in both readings, the owner of the heart; unlike not implying it, in which the described in one is the heart and in the other its owner.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {أَسْبَابَ السماوات}: Two views. One: it follows the preceding «الأسباب» as a badal or ʿaṭf bayān. Two: it is accusative by an implied "I mean". The first is better, since the original is the absence of implication.
His saying: «فَأَطَّلِعَ»: The majority read it in the nominative, conjoined to «أَبْلُغُ», so it enters the sphere of hope. Ḥafṣ and others read it in the accusative. Three views. One: it is the answer to the command in His saying «ابْنِ لي», so it is accusative by an implied «أَنْ» after the «فاء» in its answer, according to the rule of the Basrans, as in the saying:
3933 - يا ناقُ سِيْري عَنَقاً فَسِيحا ... إلى سليمانَ فَنَسْتريحا
(O she-camel, go at a wide swift pace to Sulaymān, so that we may rest.)
This best accords with the school of the Basrans. Second: it is accusative. The Shaykh said: "As a conjunction on supposition, since the khabar of «لعلَّ» has often come paired with «أنْ», often in verse and rarely in prose. Whoever put it in the accusative supposed that the nominative verb occurring as khabar is accusative by «أنْ», and conjunction on supposition is frequent, although it is not regular." End of quotation. Third: it is accusative as the answer to hope in «لعلَّ», which is a Kufan school whose adherents cited this reading and the reading of ʿĀṣim {وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يزكى أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنفَعَهُ} [ʿAbasa: 3-4], with «فتنفَعَه» accusative as an answer to «لعلَّه». al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, saying: "likening hope to wish." The Basrans refuse that, and parse the two readings as above.
In Sūrat ʿAbasa it may be the answer to the question in His saying «وما يُدريك», since it follows from it in meaning. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Ibn Jubāra al-Hudhalī said: "As the answer to wish," and there is some question about that, since there is no wish in the wording, only hope. People have distinguished between wish and hope: hope occurs only with the possible, unlike wish, which occurs with it and with the impossible, as in the saying:
3934 - لَيْتَ الشبابَ هو الرَّجيعُ على الفتى ... والشيبُ كان هو البَدِئُ الأولُ
(Would that youth were what returns to the young man, and grey hair were what came first.)
«زَيَّنَ لفرعونَ» was read in the active, the agent being Satan. The disagreement over {وَصُدَّ عَنِ السبيل} has preceded in al-Raʿd; whoever made it active omitted the object, i.e. "he turned his people from the way." Ibn Wassāb read «وصِدَّ» with kasra on the ṣād, as though he transferred the vowel of the first dāl to the first radical after supposing its vowel taken away. This has preceded in the case of «رِدَّ», and that the three dialects permissible in «قيل» and «بِيع» are allowed in it. Ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakra read «وصَدٌّ» with fatḥa on the ṣād and ḍamma with tanwīn on the dāl, making it a maṣdar conjoined to «سوءُ عملِه», i.e. "Satan made the evil of his deed and the barring attractive to him." «التَّباب» is loss; this has preceded at His saying {غَيْرَ تَتْبِيبٍ} [Hūd: 101]. The disagreement has also preceded at His saying {يَدْخُلُونَ الجنة} in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ [verse 40].

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {وياقوم}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why did he bring the «واو» in the third vocative and not the second? I say: because the second enters upon speech that is an explanation of the general and an interpretation of it, so what enters upon it was given its ruling in the impermissibility of the entry of the «واو». As for the third, it enters upon speech that is not of that standing."
His saying: {وتدعونني إِلَى النار}: This clause is resumptive; he reports this of them after his question about his own calling. The implied form may be: "and what is the matter with you that you call me to the Fire," which is the apparent view. It is weak that the clause be a ḥāl, i.e. "What is the matter with you, that I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire?"

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying: {تَدْعُونَنِي}: This clause is a badal from the first «تَدْعونني» by way of explication of it. He used a verbal clause in His saying «تَدْعُونني» to show that their calling is false and without permanence, and a nominal clause in His saying «وأنا أَدْعوكم» to show the permanence of his calling and its strength.
The disagreement over {لاَ جَرَمَ} [Ghāfir: 43] has already preceded. al-Zamakhsharī said here: "It was reported from the Arabs «لا جُرْمَ أنه يفعل كذا» with ḍamma on the jīm and sukūn on the rāʾ in the sense of «لا بُدَّ», and fuʿl and faʿal are two brothers, like «رُشْد» and «رَشَد», «عُدْم» and «عَدَم»."

semin-durr:44-44.t: His saying: {وَأُفَوِّضُ}: This is resumptive. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a ḥāl from the agent of «أَقول».

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {النار}: The majority read it in the nominative. Three views. One: it is a badal from «سوءُ العذاب». Two: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it, that is the evil of the punishment, is the Fire," because it is the answer to an implied question; and «يُعْرَضُون», on these two views, may be a ḥāl from «النار» and may be a ḥāl from «آل فرعون». Three: it is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is «يُعْرَضون». «النارَ» was also read in the accusative. Two views. One: it is accusative by an implied verb which «يُعْرَضون» interprets in meaning, i.e. "they burn in the Fire, being exposed to it," like His saying {والظالمين أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ} [al-Insān: 31]. Two: it is accusative in the sense of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ); al-Zamakhsharī said this. On the first, «يُعْرَضُون» has no position, being an interpreter; on the second, it is a ḥāl as above.
His saying: «ويومَ تقومُ»: Three views, the clearest being that it is governed by an implied saying, and that implied saying is the one in which the imperative clause «أدخِلوا» is quoted, the implied form being: "and it will be said, on the day the Hour is established: Cause to enter." Two: it is accusative by «أدخِلوا», i.e. "cause to enter on the day the Hour is established." On these two views the pause is complete at His saying «وعَشِيَّاً». Three: it is conjoined to the two adverbials before it, so it is governed by «يُعْرَضُون». On this the pause is at His saying «الساعة», and «أَدْخِلوا» is governed by an implied saying, i.e. "it will be said to them such and such."
al-Kisāʾī, Ḥamza, Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read «أدْخِلُوا» with the hamza of cutting, an imperative from «أَدْخَلَ», so «آلَ فرعون» is the first object and «أشدَّ العذاب» the second object. The others read «ادْخُلوا» with the hamza of joining, from «دَخَلَ يَدْخُلُ». So «آلَ فرعونَ» is a vocative whose particle of address has been omitted, and «أشدَّ» is accusative by it, either as an adverbial or as a direct object, i.e. "Enter, O family of Pharaoh, into the severest punishment."

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying: {وَإِذْ يَتَحَآجُّونَ}: As to the operator in «إذ», three views. One: it is conjoined to «غُدُوَّاً», so it is governed by «يُعْرَضون», i.e. "they are exposed to the Fire at all these times"; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. Two: it is conjoined to His saying {إِذِ القلوب لَدَى الحناجر} [Ghāfir: 18]; al-Ṭabarī said this. There is some question about it because of the distance between them, and because the apparent view is that the pronoun in «يَتَحاجُّون» returns to the family of Pharaoh. Three: it is accusative by an implied "Remember", which is clear.
His saying: «تَبَعاً»: Three views. One: it is a collective noun for «تابع» (follower), like «خادِم» and «خَدَم», «غائِب» and «غَيَبَ», «أَديم» and «أَدَم». Two: it is a maṣdar standing in the place of the active participle, i.e. «تابِعين». Three: it is also a maṣdar, but with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. «ذوي تَبَع».
His saying: «نصيباً»: Three views. One: it is accusative by an implied verb that His saying «مُغْنُون» indicates, the implied form being "Will you ward off from us a share." Two: «مُغْنون» is given the sense of «حامِلين» (bearing). Three: it is accusative as a maṣdar. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "As «شيءٌ» was thus. Do you not see His saying {لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلاَ أَوْلاَدُهُمْ مِّنَ الله شَيْئاً} [Āl ʿImrān: 116]? «شيْئاً» is in the place of «غَناء» (avail), so likewise «نصيباً»." «من النار» is an adjective of «نَصيباً».

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {إِنَّا كُلٌّ}: The majority read «كلٌ» in the nominative. Its nominative is as a mubtadaʾ, «فيها» is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «إنَّ».
