This is like His saying in Āl ʿImrān {قُلْ إِنَّ الأمر كُلُّهُ للَّهِ} in the reading of Abū ʿAmr. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read it in the accusative, with three views. One: it is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the noun of «إنَّ». al-Zamakhsharī said: "An emphasis of the noun of «إنَّ», which is definite; and the tanwīn is a compensation for the muḍāf ilayhi; he means: 'we, all of us, are in it'." End of quotation. That is, «فيها» is then the khabar. Ibn ʿAṭiyya also held that it is an emphasis. Ibn Mālik rejected this view and said in his Tasḥīl: "The intention of its annexation does not suffice, contrary to al-Zamakhsharī." I say: this is not the school of al-Zamakhsharī alone; it is also transmitted from the Kufans. Two: it is accusative as ḥāl. Ibn Mālik said: "The view I accept is that «كلاً» in the stated reading is accusative as a ḥāl from the nominative pronoun in «فيها», and «فيها» is the operator, and it has been fronted before it despite its non-flexibility, as it was fronted in the reading of whoever read {والسماوات مَطْوِيَّاتٍ بِيَمِينِهِ}, and like the saying of al-Nābigha:
3935 - رَهْطُ ابنِ كُوْزٍ مُحقِبيْ أَدْراعِهم ... فيهمْ ورَهْطُ ربيعةَ بنِ حُذار
(The clan of Ibn Kūz, carrying their coats of mail behind them, among them, and the clan of Rabīʿa ibn Ḥudhār.)
and the saying of one of the Ṭayyiʾites:
3936 - دعا فَأَجَبْنَا وَهْو بادِيَ ذلَّةٍ ... لديكمْ وكان النصرُ غيرَ بعيدِ
(He called and we answered, while he showed humility before you, and victory was not far.)
meaning with «باديَ» in the accusative." This is the school of al-Akhfash, but al-Zamakhsharī forbade it, saying: "If you ask: can «كلاً» be a ḥāl governed by «فيها»? I say: no, because the adverbial does not operate on a fronted ḥāl as it operates on a fronted adverbial. You say «كلَّ يوم لك ثوبٌ», but you do not say «قائماً في الدار زيد»." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "What he forbade, al-Akhfash permitted when the ḥāl is in the middle, as in «زيدٌ قائماً في الدار» and «زيدٌ قائماً عندك»; and the example he gave does not match what is in the verse, because in the verse the subject of the predication, which is the noun of «إنَّ», came first, and the ḥāl came in the middle, if we say it is a ḥāl, with its operator delayed. As for his example, 'you do not say «قائماً في الدار زيد»', both the predicate and the subject are delayed in it. Some have mentioned that the prohibition in that is by consensus of the grammarians."
I say: al-Zamakhsharī's prohibition is correct because he proceeds according to the school of the majority, and as for his illustration with what he mentioned, it does not harm him, because it is in a place of prohibition, so his not permitting it is sound.
Three: «كلاً» is a badal from «نا» in «إنَّا», for «كلاً» has been followed by operators, as if it were said "Indeed all are in it."
And since they have interpreted the saying:
2937 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . حَوْلاً أَكْتعاً ...
[and the saying:]
2938 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . وحَوْلاً أَجْمعا ...
as a badal despite the non-flexibility of «أكتع» and «أجمع», it is all the more fitting and proper in «كل». Moreover the well-known thing is the definiteness of «كل» when it is cut off. It is related, as common and widespread: «مررتُ بكلٍ قائماً وببعض جالساً», and some ascribe it to Sībawayh. The indefiniteness of «كل» and its accusative as ḥāl is extremely irregular, as in «مررت بهم كلاً», i.e. all together. If it is said: this involves a total badal from a pronoun of the present person, which is not permissible, there are two answers. One: the Kufans and al-Akhfash allow that, and they recited the saying:
3939 - أنا سيفُ العشيرةِ فاعْرِفوني ... حُمَيْداً قد تَذَّرَّيْتُ السَّناما
(I am the sword of the clan, so know me: Ḥumayd; I have climbed to the hump's summit.)
where «حُميداً» is a badal from the yā' of «اعرِفوني»; the Basrans interpreted it as accusative by ikhtiṣāṣ. Two: that what we have here is not the place of disagreement, because it indicates inclusion and comprehensiveness. They have said that whenever the badal indicates that, it is permissible, and they recited:
3940 - فما بَرِحَتْ أقدامنا في مكانِنا ... ثلاثتِنا حتى أُزِيْرُوا المنَائيا
(Our feet did not leave our place, the three of us, until they were made to visit the deaths.)
and like it His saying the Exalted {تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيداً لأَوَّلِنَا وَآخِرِنَا} [al-Māʾida: 114]. They said «ثلاثتنا» is a badal from «نا» in «مكاننا» because of its indication of inclusion, and likewise «لأوَّلنا وآخِرنا» is a badal from «نا» in «لنا»; so for that to be permissible in «كل», which is the origin in comprehensiveness and inclusion, is a fortiori. This is the speech of the Shaykh on the third view, and there is some question about it, because al-Mubarrad and Makkī stated explicitly that the badal in this verse is not permissible, so how can it be claimed that there is no disagreement over the badal, this being the case? It should not be said that in the verse there is a fourth view: that «كلاً» is an adjective of the noun of «إنَّ», for al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ stated that explicitly, saying: it is an adjective of the noun of «إنَّ», because the Kufans use the name "adjective" for emphasis and do not mean the real adjective. Among those who stated explicitly what I have said regarding the stated interpretation is Makkī, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, and because al-Kisāʾī permitted describing only the pronoun of the absent person, not the speaker or the addressee.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {يَوْماً مِّنَ العذاب}: There are two views about «يوماً». One: it is an adverbial of «يُخَفِّفْ», and the object of «يُخَفِّفْ» is omitted, i.e. "lighten for us something of the punishment in a day." According to the view of al-Akhfash, «مِنْ» may be redundant, so «العذاب» would be the object, i.e. "lighten for us on the day of punishment." Two: it is a direct object, but the day is not lightened; what is lightened is what is contained in it, so the implied form is "lighten the punishment of a day." That is unsettled given His saying «من العذاب», and saying that it is a confirming adjective like a ḥāl is more unsettled still. The apparent view is that «مِن العذاب» is the object of «يُخَفِّف», «مِنْ» is partitive, and «يوماً» is an adverbial. They asked that some of the punishment be lightened for them, not all of it, on some day, not every day or a particular day.

semin-durr:51-51.t: His saying: {وَيَوْمَ يَقُومُ الأشهاد}: The majority read «يقوم» with yā' below. Abū ʿAmr in the narration of al-Minqarī from him, Ibn Hurmuz and Ismāʿīl read it with tā' above, for the feminine of the group. «الأشهادُ» may be the plural of «شهيد», like «شَريف» and «أَشْراف», which agrees with His saying {فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جِئْنَا مِن كُلِّ أمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ} [al-Nisāʾ: 41]; or the plural of «شاهِد», like «صاحِب» and «أصحاب», which agrees with His saying {إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِداً} [al-Aḥzāb: 45].

semin-durr:52-52.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ}: a badal from the preceding «يوم», or an explication of it, or it is accusative by an implied "I mean". The disagreement over His saying «يَنْفَع الظالمين» with tā' and yā' has already preceded at the end of al-Rūm.

semin-durr:54-54.t: His saying: {هُدًى وذكرى}: Two views on both. One: they are both objects of purpose, i.e. "for the sake of guidance and remembrance." Two: they are both maṣdars in the position of ḥāl.
